title: DeliveryLane
description: One project's independent delivery lane within a DeliveryOrchestration, and the schedulable unit the worker scheduler leases and advances through waiting/blocked/runnable/leased/running/review/failed/accepted. A lane always carries its own project_id so cross-project reads and writes fail closed.

parent_task_id.description: Id of the parent task this lane delivers, assigned once the dependency graph resolves it. Empty until then.

status.description: The scheduling state machine. waiting: predecessors unresolved. blocked: an unresolved hard blocker was reported with evidence. runnable: no unresolved predecessor, no worker leased yet. leased: a worker holds an unexpired lease but has not reported starting. running: the leased worker is actively executing. review: work reported complete, awaiting review. failed: rejected, expired past retry budget, or reported failed. accepted: terminal success.

lease_worker_id.description: Worker holding the current lease; empty when not leased/running.

lease_token.description: Opaque token the leaseholder must present to heartbeat/complete/reject - proves it still holds this lease, not a stale or resumed one.

lease_expires_at.description: Lease/heartbeat deadline; past this with no renewal, the lease is expired and the lane returns to runnable.

attempt.description: Number of leases granted so far for this lane; incremented on retry.

blocked_by.description: Exact blocker ids (unresolved predecessor task ids, or a reported discovered blocker) while status is waiting or blocked.

revision.description: Optimistic-concurrency counter; incremented on every applied event.

branch.description: The lane's own git branch name, set once its worktree is first created; persists even after the worktree directory is later removed, so a later resume checks out the same branch instead of creating a new one.

worktree_path.description: Absolute path to the lane's current linked worktree directory; present only while the worktree exists on disk, cleared (but branch/base_sha/base_remote kept) when removed.

base_sha.description: The exact commit the branch was forked from.

base_remote.description: The remote name (e.g. "origin") the base branch was fetched from.

semar_record_id.description: Id of the knowledge record holding Semar's synthesis for this lane's current attempt. Cleared, along with every later stage below, whenever it is resubmitted.

gareng_record_id.description: Id of the knowledge record holding Gareng's feasibility review for this lane's current attempt. Cleared, along with petruk_record_id and bagong_record_id, whenever it is resubmitted.

petruk_record_id.description: Id of the knowledge record holding Petruk's plan for this lane's current attempt. Cleared, along with bagong_record_id, whenever it is resubmitted.

bagong_record_id.description: Id of the knowledge record holding Bagong's independent review for this lane's current attempt. A held lease cannot be completed until this is set.

pr_provider.description: Which provider the lane's published pull request lives on. Absent until a pull request has actually been published for this lane.

pr_repo_slug.description: The repository the lane's published pull request was opened against, in the provider's own repository-identifier form (e.g. "owner/repo" for GitHub).

pr_number.description: The provider's own number for the lane's published pull request. Once set, a lane never opens a second pull request for the same attempt.

pr_url.description: A link to the lane's published pull request.

repair_cycle_count.description: Number of repair cycles started for this lane so far. Absent is equivalent to zero.

escalated_at.description: When this lane was last escalated for a human to look at, e.g. after exhausting its repair-cycle budget. Absent while the lane has never been escalated. Escalation never changes the lane's own scheduling status.
